workflow: Drafting warm, professional business emails from rough notes

test_cases.input: Hi John - thanks for sending this. I looked through it and mostly aligned. Can we meet next week maybe Tuesday afternoon? Also want to confirm timeline before we move forward.
good_output_should: Rewrite the message into a warm, professional email
Preserve the thank-you message
Request a meeting for next week
Mention confirming the timeline before moving forward
Stay clear and concise

test_cases.input: Ani, thanks for the link. I lost it from fall. 4-6 weeks works for us. I’ll send form soon.
good_output_should: Rewrite the message in a polished and professional tone
Keep the friendly tone
Mention alignment on the 4-6 week timeline
State that the sender will follow up after completing the form
Improve clarity and flow

test_cases.input: Need email to vendor. say we got the files. missing 2 tabs. can they resend asap. don’t sound rude.
good_output_should: Turn rough notes into a complete email
Sound polite and professional
Clearly mention that two tabs were missing
Request a resend without sounding harsh
Keep the email concise and readable

test_cases.input: hey - running behind, can’t do today, maybe tomorrow. sorry
good_output_should: Rewrite the message into a professional email
Keep it brief
Include an apology
Suggest rescheduling for tomorrow
Avoid overly casual wording

test_cases.input: Write an email telling client their campaign underperformed because of bad targeting from previous agency. mention numbers if needed.
good_output_should: Use a professional and tactful tone
Avoid inventing numbers or unsupported claims
Avoid unnecessarily blaming language
Acknowledge that sensitive wording may require human review
Focus on clarity and professionalism
